subject: RetailQ: performance targets, qualification notes, and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@retailq.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@retailq.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: RetailQ: performance targets, qualification notes, and pilot next steps

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the performance side before we scope the pilot. I pulled the items we discussed into the attached MAP and a short SLO requirements doc (attached).

Call highlights (short):
- Primary feature: low-latency checkout validation (tokenization + fraud scoring + suggestions) called synchronously from web checkout.
- Target traffic shape: 120 req/s average during peak, expected 2x spikes for promotions (burst to ~240 req/s).
- Payloads: 900–2,500 token window (mostly 1,200–1,800 tokens).
- Desired SLOs: p50 ~80ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 <= 320ms for end-to-end 1-token-per-chunk streaming path.
- Concurrency: target steady-state concurrency 40–60 active user sessions; sporadic spikes to 150.

Proposed cost/perf levers we recommend evaluating in pilot:
1) Continuous batching with short max latency bound (20–30ms) to improve GPU utilization without exceeding p95.
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated product/context keys (we saw 25–40% token cache-hit potential from your sample).
3) Model variants: primary = quantized 4-bit Llama-variant for bulk; fallback = 8-bit or distilled variant for tail requests to meet p99.
4) Dynamic routing & graceful degradation: route non-critical inference (background rerank, suggestions) to cheaper capacity pool.
5) Token-level streaming vs chunked streaming trade: using 1-token streaming yields lower tail but higher overhead; we suggest 4-token micro-chunks to balance latency and throughput.

Please confirm the SLO goals above (p50/p95/p99), and share: 1) a representative sample of 200 real payloads (anonymized), and 2) an internal acceptance checklist for the pilot (what constitutes pass/fail).

Next steps (proposed):
- RetailQ: drop sample payloads to the Drive link and the acceptance checklist by EOD Tue 7/14.
- Redwood: bench initial baseline (no caching, 4-bit quant) and share perf matrix by Fri 7/16.
- Joint sync to review results and pick lever combinations week of 7/19.

Attachments: RetailQ_MAP_v1.xlsx, slo_requirements.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m point if it helps.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@retailq.com>

Date: 2026-07-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RetailQ: performance targets, qualification notes, and pilot next steps

Thanks Aisha — quick clarifications from our side:
- The p99 target is for the full end-to-end web latency (includes network + client render). Is Redwood's SLO measurement typically server-side only? We may need to account for ~40–60ms client/network in our acceptance criteria.
- For streaming: our checkout flow shows customers expect incremental suggestions within ~150ms perceived time; if micro-chunks of 4 tokens add jitter, that could be visible. Can you quantify expected perceived delay for 4-token micro-chunks vs 1-token streaming?
- Budget: we have a notional cap for the pilot spend. Can you provide a rough cost delta for 4-bit quant + caching vs baseline 8-bit? A ballpark per-100k requests would be helpful.

Liam / @Marcus / @Karthik — FYI.

Priya
Product Manager, RetailQ

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@retailq.com>, Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@retailq.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RetailQ: performance targets, qualification notes, and pilot next steps

Priya — great questions, answered inline and looping in Karthik/Ben to validate engineering assumptions.

1) SLO measurement: Redwood reports server-side inference latency (time from request received by the inference endpoint to last token emitted). To map to your end-to-end target, add estimated network/client overhead. If you want, Redwood can add a synthetic proxy to measure client-to-server RTT during the pilot and produce end-to-end estimates.

2) Perceived delay (1-token vs 4-token micro-chunks):
- 1-token streaming: best perceived immediacy but increases per-token RPC overhead; p99 tail tends to be higher for high concurrency.
- 4-token micro-chunks: amortizes RPC cost and reduces GPU kernel throughput overhead; in our internal testing with similar payload shapes we saw perceived-first-byte within ~70–110ms and steady throughput improvements of ~18–30% vs 1-token streaming. We'll include breakdown in the bench results.

3) Ballpark cost delta (very rough):
- Baseline (8-bit) without caching: X units / 100k reqs (we'll provide concrete $ after we run traces).
- 4-bit quant + KV prefix caching: expect ~30–45% reduction in per-token GPU time; for workloads with 25% cache hit we typically report ~25% unit-cost reduction. Exact numbers depend on secret-sauce model kernels and sequence length distribution.

Karthik / Ben — can you confirm we can schedule a 2-day bench (baseline + 4-bit + caching + fallback path tests) once RetailQ provides the 200 payloads? Also confirm we can surface per-request p50/p95/p99 + token throughput and GPU-utilization metrics in the bench report.

Thanks — I’ll prepare a simple bench plan and timeline after you confirm availability.

— Aisha

- Deliverable: perf matrix (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, GPU util, and a short table mapping lever combinations (batch size / caching / quant) to cost delta.

Thanks all — sounds good. Priya and I chatted and we can get the 200 anonymized payloads and the acceptance checklist into the Drive link by tomorrow EOD. We agree to the proposed bench window Wed/Thu next week.

Acceptance checklist (high level):
- Server-side p95 <= 200ms for baseline path and <= 180ms for quant+caching path
- No request-level errors at >0.1% during steady-run (10k sec window)
- Verified fallback path for requests that exceed max sequence length or fail quant path
- Cost projection for 100k requests for both baseline and optimized levers

We are OK to proceed with the pilot scope you proposed — please share the bench plan and any temporary credentials/config necessary.

Liam
Head of Integrations, RetailQ
